Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)

Required findings: Symptoms include significant daily pain causing clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam demonstrates ANY of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor deficit (e.g., biceps/triceps weakness), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver), or unremitting radicular pain without concordant objective findings

Plain cervical X-rays (including flexion/extension) and advanced imaging confirm successful prior decompression/fusion; MRI/CT shows neural compression at requested level concordant with symptoms/exam caused by herniated disc, synovial/arachnoid cyst, stenosis, or osteophytes

Less than clinically meaningful improvement after at least TWO of the following conservative therapies for six (6) weeks each (unless contraindicated): prescription analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs, provider-directed exercise program, or epidural steroid/selective nerve root block at the same level

Greater than six (6) months since prior surgery; absence of unmanaged significant mental/behavioral health disorders; nicotine-free status verified as never-smoker or 6-week cessation validated by objective cotinine testing (serum/urine/saliva) within normal lab range
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.7: Adjacent Segment Disease > Radiculopathy (TOC: S12.1.1)

Required findings: Symptoms include ANY of: upper/lower extremity weakness/numbness/pain, fine motor dysfunction (buttoning, handwriting, clumsiness), gait disturbance, new-onset bowel/bladder dysfunction, or frequent falls

Physical exam demonstrates ANY of: abnormal grip and release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, positive Hoffmann sign, positive Babinski sign, tandem walking test demonstrating ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone/spasticity, clonus, or myelopathic hand

MRI/CT shows cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis concordant with symptoms and physical exam findings; plain X-rays and advanced imaging must also confirm successful prior decompression/fusion at the adjacent level
Conservative management trial is not explicitly mandated for myelopathy per policy text, but all other general criteria must be met

Greater than six (6) months since prior surgery; absence of unmanaged significant mental/behavioral health disorders; nicotine-free status verified as never-smoker or 6-week cessation validated by objective cotinine testing (serum/urine/saliva) within normal lab range
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.7: Adjacent Segment Disease > Myelopathy (TOC: S12.1.2)

Non-Indications: Surgery requested less than 6 months after prior cervical decompression or fusion at an adjacent level
Absence of concordant objective imaging (MRI/CT) demonstrating neural compression or spinal cord compression/stenosis at the requested surgical level
Failure to complete or derive clinically meaningful improvement from at least two conservative management modalities for a minimum of 6 weeks (for radiculopathy cases)
Active tobacco or nicotine use without verified 6-week cessation via objective cotinine testing
Presence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders, including major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, or substance use disorders
Imaging failure to demonstrate successful decompression and fusion at the previous operative level
Lack of documented neurological deficits, functional impairment, or myelopathic symptoms required by policy
Important criteria & exceptions: Procedure is only covered for degenerative segments adjacent to a previously operated level when ALL associated criteria are met
Conservative care trial requires at least two distinct modalities maintained for a minimum of 6 weeks each, unless medically contraindicated

Nicotine cessation must be objectively verified via serum, urinary, or salivary cotinine testing within the normal reference range for the specific laboratory, or documented as a lifelong never-smoker
Prior surgical level must show radiographic evidence of successful decompression and fusion on both plain radiographs and advanced imaging
Behavioral health and substance use disorders must be actively managed and documented as stable prior to surgical authorization
Documentation required: Operative report from prior cervical decompression or fusion procedure
Plain cervical spine X-rays including flexion/extension lateral views
Cervical MRI and/or CT radiology reports demonstrating neural compression or spinal cord compression/stenosis concordant with clinical symptoms

Pharmacy dispensing records and clinical notes documenting ≥6 weeks of conservative management (prescription analgesics/NSAIDs/steroids/gabapentinoids, physical therapy/exercise program, and/or epidural steroid/nerve root blocks)
Objective laboratory cotinine test results (serum, urine, or saliva) verifying nicotine-free status for ≥6 weeks, or formal documentation of never-smoker status
Behavioral health or psychiatric evaluation note confirming absence of unmanaged mental health or substance use disorders
Detailed physical examination notes documenting specific neurological deficits (sensory, motor, reflex changes, or myelopathic signs)
